title: Review: Functional groups: Classification of organic compounds; Measuring enthalpy changes; Energy cycles in reactions

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Reaction coordinate
items.clue: The quantity on the x-axis of an energy profile.

items.label: Temperature
items.clue: A measure of the average kinetic energy of the particles of a substance.

items.label: Hess’s law
items.clue: The enthalpy change for a reaction is independent of the pathway between the initial and final states.

questions.stem: For the reaction P → Q, where P and Q are two substances, ΔH = −60 kJ mol⁻¹. Which statement about the reaction is correct?

options.text: P has the greater potential energy, so it is the more stable of the two.
Q has more potential energy than P, so P is the more stable substance.
Because ΔH is negative, the reaction's energy profile has no energy barrier.
P has more potential energy than Q, so Q is the more stable of the two substances.

questions.explanation: ΔH is negative, so the system loses energy as P turns into Q: Q lies 60 kJ mol⁻¹ below P. The substance with the lower potential energy is the more stable, so Q is more stable than P.

questions.stem: 4.00 g of ammonium nitrate, NH₄NO₃, is dissolved in 50.0 g of water in a polystyrene cup. The temperature of the water falls from 21.60 °C to 15.40 °C. Assume that all the energy absorbed comes from the water, c(water) = 4.18 J g⁻¹ K⁻¹, and that no energy is exchanged with the air. A_r values: H 1.01, N 14.01, O 16.00. What is ΔH for dissolving ammonium nitrate?

options.text: −25.9 kJ mol⁻¹
+2.07 kJ mol⁻¹
+25.9 kJ mol⁻¹
−1.30 kJ mol⁻¹

questions.stem: Ethene reacts with hydrogen: C₂H₄(g) + H₂(g) → C₂H₆(g). Average bond enthalpies / kJ mol⁻¹: C=C 614; C–C 346; C–H 414; H–H 436. What is the enthalpy change of this reaction calculated from these data?

options.text: +124 kJ mol⁻¹
+290 kJ mol⁻¹
−124 kJ mol⁻¹
−560 kJ mol⁻¹

questions.explanation: Bonds broken: C=C + H–H = 614 + 436 = 1050 kJ mol⁻¹. Bonds formed: C–C + 2 C–H = 346 + 2(414) = 1174 kJ mol⁻¹. ΔH = 1050 − 1174 = −124 kJ mol⁻¹. The four C–H bonds already in ethene are unchanged and can be left out.

questions.stem: The boiling points of the first five straight-chain alkanes are: methane −162 °C, ethane −89 °C, propane −42 °C, butane −1 °C and pentane 36 °C. Which statement about this trend is correct?

options.text: Each further CH₂ unit adds the same rise as the last, 37 °C, so hexane is expected to boil at 73 °C.
The rise is caused by hydrogen bonding, which grows as H atoms are added to the chain.
The rise per CH₂ unit shrinks along the series, so hexane is expected to boil below 73 °C.
The rise occurs because longer molecules have more C–C and C–H bonds to break.

questions.stem: What is the IUPAC name of CH₃CH₂CH(CH₃)CH₂Cl?

options.text: 1-chloro-2-methylbutane
4-chloro-3-methylbutane
1-chloro-2-ethylpropane
2-methyl-1-chlorobutane

questions.explanation: The longest chain has four carbon atoms (butane). Numbering from the CH₂Cl end gives the locant set {1, 2}, lower than {3, 4} from the other end. Prefixes are written alphabetically: 1-chloro-2-methylbutane.

questions.stem: Which statement about the compound (CH₃)₃CNH₂ is correct?

options.text: It is a tertiary amine, as the C bonded to N carries three CH₃ groups.
It is a secondary amine, as its N atom is bonded to two H atoms.
It is a primary amine, as its N atom is bonded to one C atom.
It is an amide, since an –NH₂ group is bonded to its C atom.

questions.explanation: Amines are classified by the number of carbon atoms bonded to the nitrogen atom. Here the nitrogen is bonded to one carbon (and two H atoms), so the compound is a primary amine.

questions.stem: Why is the C–H bond enthalpy in a table of bond enthalpies described as an average value?

options.text: It is the mean of repeated measurements made on a single compound, taken to reduce the random error in the data.
The energy to break a C–H bond varies from one compound to another, so a mean over many compounds is given.
Values measured in the solid, liquid and gas are pooled into one mean, as the same C–H bonds are present in all three.
Every C–H bond has the same strength; 'average' only means the single measured value has been rounded.

questions.explanation: A C–H bond in methane, ethane or ethanol has a slightly different bond enthalpy because the rest of the molecule affects it. The tabulated value is the mean over many compounds, which is why calculations with it give estimates.

questions.stem: What is the IUPAC name of CH₂=CHCH₂CH₂OH?

options.text: but-1-en-4-ol
but-3-en-1-ol
but-4-en-1-ol
but-3-en-1-al

questions.explanation: The chain has four carbon atoms. The –OH group, named by the suffix -ol, takes the lowest locant, 1. The C=C bond is then between carbons 3 and 4 and takes the lower number, 3: but-3-en-1-ol.

questions.stem: Which compound is a structural isomer of butan-1-ol, CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂OH?

options.text: CH₃CH₂OCH₂CH₃
CH₃CH₂CH₂CHO
HOCH₂CH₂CH₂CH₃
CH₃(CH₂)₄OH

questions.explanation: Ethoxyethane is C₄H₁₀O, the same molecular formula as butan-1-ol, but its atoms are connected differently (an alkoxy group instead of a hydroxyl group). It is a functional group isomer.

questions.stem: Which compound is a secondary halogenoalkane?

options.text: (CH₃)₂CBrCH₂CH₃
CH₃CH₂CHBrCH₂CH₃
CH₃CH₂CH₂CHBr₂
CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₂Br

questions.explanation: In 3-bromopentane the carbon carrying the Br atom is bonded to two other carbon atoms (two CH₂ groups), so the compound is a secondary halogenoalkane.

questions.stem: A sample of 3-methylhexane, CH₃CH₂CH(CH₃)CH₂CH₂CH₃, is a racemic mixture. Which statement about the sample is correct?

options.text: It contains equal amounts of the cis and trans isomers of 3-methylhexane.
Its molecules are achiral, which is why the sample shows no optical activity.
It contains equal amounts of the two enantiomers of 3-methylhexane.
Fractional distillation separates it into its two enantiomers.

questions.explanation: A racemic mixture contains equal amounts of the two enantiomers. Carbon 3 of 3-methylhexane is chiral (bonded to H, CH₃, C₂H₅ and C₃H₇), so the compound exists as a pair of enantiomers, which rotate plane-polarized light equally in opposite directions.

questions.stem: The mass spectrum of pentan-3-one, CH₃CH₂COCH₂CH₃ (M_r = 86), has a molecular ion peak at m/z 86 and a peak at m/z 57. Fragment data: m/z 29 = C₂H₅⁺ or CHO⁺; m/z 57 = C₄H₉⁺ or C₂H₅CO⁺. Which species is responsible for the peak at m/z 57?

options.text: the ion C₂H₅CO⁺, left when C₂H₅ (mass 29) is lost from the molecular ion
the ion C₂H₅⁺, left behind when a fragment of mass 57 is lost
an impurity of M_r 57 in the sample, as pure pentan-3-one gives only M⁺
the ion C₄H₉⁺, since the data table lists m/z 57 as C₄H₉⁺

questions.explanation: Breaking the bond between the carbonyl carbon and one ethyl group gives C₂H₅CO⁺ (m/z 57) and an uncharged C₂H₅ fragment of mass 29 (86 − 57 = 29). Only the charged fragment is detected.

questions.stem: Carbon dioxide and water vapour are greenhouse gases, but nitrogen and oxygen are not. Which statement explains this difference?

options.text: CO₂ and H₂O are polar molecules, but N₂ and O₂ are non-polar molecules.
Vibrations of CO₂ and H₂O change their dipole moment, so they absorb IR.
Like the ozone layer, CO₂ and H₂O absorb the Sun's ultraviolet radiation.
CO₂ and H₂O reflect infrared radiation back to Earth, but N₂ and O₂ do not.

questions.explanation: A molecule absorbs infrared radiation when a vibration changes its dipole moment. CO₂ (asymmetric stretch and bending) and H₂O have such vibrations and absorb infrared radiation emitted by the Earth's surface. N₂ and O₂ have none.

questions.stem: A compound, C₂H₄O₂, is either ethanoic acid, CH₃COOH, or methyl methanoate, HCOOCH₃. Its ¹H NMR spectrum shows two singlets, at δ 2.1 and δ 11.5. Typical chemical shifts: R–COOH 9.0–13.0 ppm; H on a carbon bonded to the singly bonded O of an ester, –C(=O)–O–CH₃, 3.7–4.8 ppm. Which conclusion is correct?

options.text: Methyl methanoate: its two H environments give two singlets.
Methyl methanoate: an O–H proton gives no signal, so the acid gives one.
Ethanoic acid: δ 11.5 is the CH₃ group, as it has the most H atoms.
Ethanoic acid: δ 11.5 is the COOH proton and δ 2.1 is the CH₃ group.

questions.explanation: A signal at δ 11.5 lies in the range for R–COOH, 9.0–13.0 ppm, and methyl methanoate has no hydrogen in that range. The CH₃ group of ethanoic acid gives the singlet at δ 2.1.

questions.stem: In a high-resolution ¹H NMR spectrum, one signal is split into a quartet. What does this show about the structure?

options.text: The carbon atom(s) adjacent to the group carry three hydrogen atoms in total.
The group giving the signal is a CH₃ group, since its three H atoms give 3 + 1 = 4 peaks.
The carbon atom giving the signal is bonded to three other carbon atoms in the chain.
The environment giving the signal contains four equivalent hydrogen atoms.

questions.explanation: By the n + 1 rule, four peaks means n = 3 hydrogen atoms on the adjacent carbon atom(s), for example a CH₂ group next to a CH₃ group. The number of hydrogen atoms in the group itself is shown by the area, not the splitting.
